thread:
pagerduty-bot: ALERT -> high error-rate detected for /v1/generate in eu-west-1 (p50 latency spike, 5xxs). Escalation: P1. Paging olivia (on-call).
olivia: on it. grabbing logs + routing traces. any customer-facing impact? cc @devon for infra.
devon: seeing spillover to us-east-1 in the routing table — a bunch of eu requests ended up routed to a fallback pool. Not sure why policy chose fallback over queueing. Linking initial trace: https://internal.logs/replay/2061234567
kevin: I can pull model fallback decisions from the router. running:
```
curl -s 'https://routers/api/decisions?trace=2061234567' | jq '.decisions[] | {ts, route, fallback, reason}'
```
Got a lot of `fallback_model: small-quant-v2` entries for requests > 2048 tokens.
lucy: small-quant-v2 is quantized and missing some attention kernels; we saw degraded correctness earlier but not full 5xxs. Are the 5xxs from the model or the serving runtime? Logs show both `kvcache_miss` and `unsupported_kernel` in the same window.
maria: timeline from metrics:
- 2061234500 increase in avg seq_len from a traffic campaign
- 2061234523 router policy triggers region fallback due to perceived capacity shortfall
- 2061234550 many requests hit `small-quant-v2` fallback
- 2061234575 error spike (502/503) and increased latency
olivia: mitigation applied at 2061234620: pinned routing to eu-west primary pool and disabled automatic fallback for that route. Observing drop in 5xxs but still elevated p95. Customers with long-context requests may have had truncation or errors. Customer-impact estimate: 6 customer tenants affected, mostly high-context prompts (search/agent workloads).
devon: logs attached (snippets):
```
[2061234569] router: decision=FALLBACK -> pool=dedicated-fallback-eu small-quant-v2 reason="capacity_threshold"
[2061234572] runtime: model=small-quant-v2 error=unsupported_kernel opcode=attn_causal
[2061234576] runtime: session=abc123 5xx=ModelExecutionError cause="kernel_fail"
```
kevin: hypothesis 1: fallback policy incorrectly matched traffic signature (seq_len estimate off) and routed long-context requests to quantized model that doesn't support the attention kernel -> model execution error -> 5xx. Hypothesis 2: primary eu cluster had transient node oom causing capacity shortfall and router decided fallback; the fallback pool was mis-tagged as compatible for long-context but actually limited.
lucy: adding hypothesis 3: KV cache behavior — when a request is sent to fallback, the KV cache is empty and runtime code path tries to allocate larger KV buffers and hits an untested kernel path. That would explain simultaneous kvcache_miss + unsupported_kernel.
maria: collecting per-request traces to validate kernel path. I've pushed a query to trace-store for span 'kernel_select' between 2061234540-2061234590.
olivia: current mitigation remains: 1) routing pin for eu-west, 2) disable `auto-fallback` for routes serving >1024 tokens, 3) increase alerting sensitivity for model kernel errors. Need owners for RCA doc and action items.
devon: I'll own infra action: check primary eu nodes for OOM/evictions and restore capacity labels if wrong. ETA 2 hours.
kevin: I'll validate router policy code path and fallback pool compatibility matrix. If pool labels were stale (e.g., supports_long_context=false but reachable), that's a config bug. ETA 4 hours.
lucy: I'll run regressions on small-quant-v2 in a staging loop to verify kernel availability for sequences up to 4096; also check quantization packaging. ETA 6 hours.
olivia: quick note for customer comms: brief heads-up already posted to status with "degraded generation for some EU customers due to routing fallback; mitigation applied". We should draft follow-up once RCA is clearer. @maria follow up with exact tenant list and Affected_window.
maria: tenant list: tenant-a, tenant-k, tenant-ops, tenant-research, tenant-legacy, tenant-eu-saas. Affected_window: 2061234550-2061234620 (70s). Sending CSV to #customer-impact.
deploybot: Deploy detected: router-config v2.14 promoted at 2061234401 across eu-west. No rollbacks yet.
olivia: interesting — config change before incident. devon/maria can you correlate router-config rollout with capacity labels? Could be a bad rollout.
devon: yes, I'm seeing that v2.14 reset a couple of pool labels related to `supports_long_context` due to a defaulting bug. That would immediately mark fallback pool as eligible for long-context. This lines up with the chain.
kevin: confirmed. reproduction locally: when `supports_long_context` missing, fallback selector treats it as `true`. That is the policy bug. Patch idea: make selector default to false and add unit tests.
lucy: prioritizing an urgent test and plan: 1) unit test for fallback selector, 2) add E2E that simulates long seq routing to quantized pool and checks kernel support, 3) add a runtime guard that refuses model exec when kernel unsupported (fail early with clearer error code).
olivia: action items summarized (in-thread):
- infra (devon): check and reconcile pool labels, audit rollout v2.14 (OWNER: devon, ETA: 2h)
- router (kevin): patch selector default + hotfix for config (OWNER: kevin, ETA: 3h)
- runtime (lucy): add E2E/regression + guard for unsupported_kernel (OWNER: lucy, ETA: 6h)
- cs (maria): customer list + targeted comms + post-incident notice (OWNER: maria, ETA: 4h)
- oncall (olivia): draft RCA skeleton, coordinate handoff to postmortem channel (OWNER: olivia, ETA: 8h)
maria: customer comm draft attached to #customer-impact, please review before send. Suggest apologizing, timeframe, mitigation, and next steps for prevention.
olivia: one more note — we saw 3 tenants retrying aggressively which amplified spillover. Let's add a rate-limiter recommendation for retries in the router (soft backoff). kevin add to backlog.
kevin: added ticket INF-4921: router: default fallback selector -> false + retry-backoff config. link: https://issues/internal/INF-4921
devon: infra findings: no OOMs in primary after 2061234600; capacity shortfall was due to transient label mismatch after config rollout. I'm reverting the rollout to previous stable on eu-west to be safe.
olivia: thanks. once devon reverts and kevin patches, we should reopen the canary pipeline and run a controlled rollout with stricter label validation.
ulla: (system) incident severity reduced to P2 at 2061234702 after 5xxs dropped below threshold.
olivia: ok handoff: SRE on-call from 2061234800 is devon. I'm logging a follow-up RCA meeting at 2061239000 in #postmortems. Please add any dry-run notes and logs to the doc.
kevin: saving decision logs and example request ids to the RCA doc: request ids: rq_8f1a, rq_8f1b, rq_8f2c. I'll paste kernel_select spans in the postmortem.
lucy: plan to include model compatibility matrix and recommended labeling scheme for pools in the RCA.
maria: I'll coordinate customer follow-ups after RCA is drafted. Draft link: https://docs.internal/incident-2061234567
olivia: closing live mitigation. keep this thread for in-incident RCA coordination. If anyone finds additional hypotheses, add them here with evidence. :white_check_mark:
